# Model candidates

`app/cards/model_candidates.py` is a mutable, pipeline-compatible downstream
review/selection card. It consumes `proxy_data.tuning_results`, never private UI
table state. `app/model_review.py` contains pure evidence-construction, diagnostics,
shortlist, Pareto and chart helpers. Statistical eligibility/posteriors reuse
`pipeline_comparison`; no complexity or ensemble logic is added.

## Evidence and lifecycle

Search specs declare `prediction_evidence: 2`. During a fold, only numeric
validation losses needed for exact repeat-wise P95/exceedance calculations are
written to a unique compressed temporary file. Classification label errors are
counts; probability matrices are reduced immediately to per-observation log loss.
No predictions, outcomes, row positions, class matrices or fitted models persist.
Fold metadata contains count, timing, kind, and (while unfinished) checksum/key,
maximum and a context hash binding the file to the search/trial/fold.

Completed trials replace file references with bounded summaries: P95 for regression,
classification error rate/log loss, a maximum and 101 exceedance proportions.
Thresholds are generated from the maximum rather than redundantly stored. At most
one repeat's validation losses is materialized during finalization. Files retire
only after the parent applies the corresponding completion update, preventing a
configuration-save race with stale partial state. Failure/reset/session cleanup
also remove owned files; cancellation prunes unpublished files by worker namespace.
Direct-library runs clean completed files synchronously; temporary cache roots
are removed at process exit.

`portable_checkpoint` embeds only pending compressed arrays at explicit save/export
boundaries. `restore_checkpoint` validates hashes/archive headers and rekeys each
import, so switching configurations never relies on a prior session's files or
shares file ownership. Completed configurations are file-free. The emscripten
backend holds compressed pending bytes and never accesses native paths. Generic
restored state is consumed once to release its duplicate bookmark copy. Large
browser configuration staging uses an isolated IndexedDB store and a small
sessionStorage token; records are consumed on restoration, with abandoned records
pruned after a day. Native fitting remains unavailable in shinylive. A saved source signature
allows file-free read-only review of completed archives when that signature
matches but native fitting/search validation is unavailable. Read-only results
cannot be accepted as a pipeline. Missing native estimators use recorded scalar
choices for parameter differences, without importing or deserializing models.

The worker update queue has capacity two and carries only changed trial records
and scalar status/RNG headers. The UI merges those deltas into its history; it
never queues deep copies of an accumulated prediction history. Completed-review
invalidation uses a revision hash rather than a second retained history snapshot.
Downstream evidence stores one unfitted template per method, sharing trial scalar
choices with history, and constructs a trial pipeline on demand. No tuning
acceptance is needed for evidence export. Legacy row lists are stripped without
first duplicating them; old scores remain visible but implementation changes
require a new search for current diagnostics/resume compatibility.

`proxy_data` stores an immutable-by-ownership evidence record with a signature of
the clean data, roles, modelling context, evaluation plan and shared preprocessing.
Public getters copy evidence/pipelines defensively. Successors preserve it but the
getter rejects incompatible state; explicit estimator replacement clears it.
Clone/equality account for it. Explicit accepted tuning/review selections rebase
the signature to their selected preprocessing while preserving the original
search provenance. Review acceptance clones the stored full pipeline, records
`model_candidates` lineage, and never fits it.

## Review semantics

Shortlists retain top N completed configurations independently per model method.
A stable earliest-ID best-scoring reference is identified within each method.
Paired comparisons require complete matching fold IDs and upstream repeated,
shuffled ordinary/stratified CV. Nonreference rows are practically equivalent,
meaningfully worse or inconclusive; the reference has no fictitious equivalence
probability. A positive tolerance and decision probability are explicit controls.
Zero paired variance remains unavailable. Selection bias is stated.

Regression tail diagnostics concatenate validation absolute errors within each
repeat, compute each repeat's P95, then average. Classification error rates and
log losses average repeat summaries; probabilities retain class alignment. Timing
is warm validation-batch point/label prediction throughput, including preprocessing,
with explicit concurrency/batch/hardware limitations. No uncertainty claim treats
repeats as independent datasets. Exceedance curves average per-repeat curves and
use a common classification loss type for all displayed representatives.

Between-method views choose one representative per method, initially its score
reference. Two selected numerical axes define a Pareto frontier with proper score,
risk and speed directions; incomplete measurements cannot receive frontier status.
Interpretability remains a qualitative description. Treatment-role guidance does
not imply causal identification. Chart clicks and flip-side row selection share
candidate identity. A same-method comparison selector supports arbitrary pairs
for parameter differences. Representative changes are diagnostic; acceptance is explicit.
Footer actions and the comparison download use the standard rounded primary
buttons. Download is 220 pixels wide with the standard file-arrow-down icon.
Best-score reference rows use emphasized text without changing their background.
Selection opens the parameter details panel; explicit deselection closes it.
Grid rebuilds preserve trial identity rather than treating their transient empty
selection as a user deselection. The parameter comparison fills the card width and wraps its first column,
overriding the shared 180-pixel truncation rule locally. Model parameter labels use
the method display name without its regression/classification suffix, followed by
a hyphen-separated estimator path. Search/checkpoint keys are unchanged. Status,
selection details and eligibility messages are concise; explanatory cautions live
in the Quarto help rather than repeated output text.
Representatives/acceptance restore only against matching search identity. The
exported evidence also records the shortlist, representative IDs, tolerance,
decision probability and accepted ID under a versioned review entry. Tables
round displayed numeric values to three decimals; CSV retains full precision.

## Validation

Unit tests cover held-out row alignment, no holdout access, cloning, acceptance,
evidence invalidation, per-method shortlists, non-equivalence without tolerance,
repeat-aware tails, regression/classification diagnostics, Pareto directions,
missing evidence and parameter differences. Browser tests cover the review views,
representative persistence, acceptance/revert and tuning evidence export.

Model review, pipeline-tuning history and Data journey each retain one FigureWidget
per session and update its data/layout in place. Closing replaced models alone
did not prevent WebKit content-process memory growth during repeated widget-view
construction. WidgetSlot closes the retained widget on session end and remains a
fallback for explicit replacement. History retains existing method traces across
updates. A WebKit regression requires repeated review changes to open no new
widget models. Fullscreen modebar changes update the existing plot configuration.
